archiveTitle: The Royal Purchases of One Lady of the Elven Court
notice: 19 individually identified original generated Daysha illustrations are published. If Daysha wears a finished gown in approved story art, she has purchased it; only prices, dates, and possible matching of repeated gowns may remain open. Source references and rejected versions are excluded.

subjects: Daysha's mother (blue-haired birth mother; separate from Rome's mother)

garments.title: Blooming Meadow Sapphire-and-Gold Gown
garments.notes: Original generated portrait of Daysha wearing a purchased gown in a flowing white, lavender, gold and sapphire floral gown.

garments.title: Ice-Blue Floral Court Gown
garments.notes: Distinct ice-blue floral, embroidered court gown. Later family scenes share a blue floral visual motif, although matching them to the exact same physical gown remains to be reconciled.

garments.title: Roseblush Floral Ombré Gown
garments.notes: White pleated crossover bodice and straps, soft blush-to-coral layered tulle skirt, floral pink appliqués cascading from the waist. Seen on the mannequin during a chocolate delivery and then fitted on Daysha by the resident elven master seamstress. The two scenes depict one physical gown; the acquisition is canon; exact date and price remain to be assigned.

garments.title: Pearlescent Manaweave Floral Gown
garments.notes: Second distinct gown of the same atelier visit as the Roseblush gown. A new mana-infused pearlescent fabric, shimmering icy blue, lavender, silver and delicate iridescent white floral motifs; Daysha displays it with an ornate blue-violet crystal crown without dangling adornments. The shop master is delighted to introduce the fabric to the Queen. Purchase canon; exact date and gold value remain to be assigned.

garments.title: Midnight Sapphire Starfall Gown
garments.notes: Queen Daysha tries on a midnight-sapphire, constellation-sparkling full-skirt gown with silver crystal strands, jeweled waist, transparent draped sleeves, and richly layered train. Accompanied by her blue-haired birth mother (distinct from King Rome's silver-haired mother-in-law) in the all-elven Gilded Spindle boutique. The silver-haired master seamstress, red-haired hem artisan, another elven worker, and Garrick Vellmont are present. One purchased garment; date and paid-gold valuation remain open.

garments.title: Icesilk and Midnight-Blue Mantle Court Gown
garments.notes: A distinct ice-blue fitted gown with sapphire-dark embroidered mantle, revealed at the Golden Spindle with Lady Liana. The same outing begins with Daysha wearing an earlier pale-blue gown; that arrival appearance alone is not a second purchased design. Purchase canon; date and paid-gold valuation remain open.

garments.title: Royal Sapphire Starfire Halter Gown
garments.notes: Royal-blue fitted gown with jeweled silver halter neckline, crystal-star detailing and sweeping train. Daysha has purchased it at the Golden Spindle before a masked ambush at her carriage. Flaming sword pierces a foe made of smoke. One purchased garment; the source mannequin photograph is excluded.

sceneSequences.title: Estelle's council-chamber ambush
sceneSequences.description: Princess Estelle throws a magical glitter-filled water balloon from the rafters at King Rome during a council gathering. The balloon has burst against his head; her throwing hand is empty as the court laughs. This final continuity-corrected illustration supersedes the earlier version with a balloon still in hand.

sceneSequences.description: Rome recovers from the glitter prank in the playroom with two Maine Coons; Daysha performs the cleaning spell, then the family walks towards the courtyard.

sceneSequences.title: Chocolates for the seamstresses and the Roseblush fitting
sceneSequences.description: Daysha arrives at the all-elven royal boutique bearing chocolates for the hardworking staff. She discovers a newly completed white-to-pink floral gown on the mannequin, eagerly tries it on, and the newly resident silver-haired master seamstress adjusts its waist while the other elves watch. These are consecutive scenes of the same gown, not separate gown purchases.

sceneSequences.description: After the chocolates and Roseblush fitting, Daysha tries the boutique's second gown of the day: a radiant, mana-infused pearlescent fabric newly introduced by the elven master seamstress. The shop master proudly presents her invention. Crown revisions are one finalized scene, not additional dress purchases.

sceneSequences.title: The Midnight Star fitting with Daysha's mother
sceneSequences.description: At the Gilded Spindle, Queen Daysha tries on a midnight-sapphire gown cascading with crystal constellations. Her own blue-haired mother assists while Garrick Vellmont and the atelier's established elven seamstresses complete the fitting. This is the final corrected image; previous drafts are excluded. Daysha's finished gown is a canonical purchase; the precise gold amount and calendar day have not yet been assigned.
sceneSequences.purchaseMeaning: Daysha wears gowns she has purchased. Scene repeats do not charge her husband a second time.

sceneSequences.title: Lady Liana's first visit to the Golden Spindle
sceneSequences.description: Queen Daysha meets Lady Liana, the golden-haired sister of Rome's mother, the Queen Dowager, while going to the Golden Spindle. Lady Liana joins her in midnight-blue finery and watches the workshop elves fit Daysha's new ice-blue court gown and sapphire-dark mantle. Two illustrations of one outing; only the fitting establishes a new gown design, the new finished gown is canonically acquired by Daysha, with final pricing/date still to be assigned.
sceneSequences.purchaseMeaning: Daysha wears gowns she has purchased. Scene repeats do not charge her husband a second time.

sceneSequences.title: Smoke in the carriage courtyard
sceneSequences.description: After buying the royal-blue starfire gown, Queen Daysha and her guards are attacked by masked assailants at the carriage outside the Golden Spindle. The Queen wields her flaming blade using her long adventuring experience, but her first target turns out to be made of smoke. A separate purchased gown from the preceding Saturday fitting; the mannequin reference is excluded.

accounting.policy: Every finished gown worn by Daysha in approved story art is canonically purchased. One physical dress counts once; repeat scenes and correction images do not create another transaction. Unknown exact gold and calendar dates remain open accounting fields, not doubts about acquisition.

purchaseCanon.rule: An approved original illustration showing Queen Daysha wearing a finished gown is canonical evidence that she has purchased/acquired that gown. This is a story fact, not a provisional inference dependent on a recovered cash receipt.
purchaseCanon.countRule: Each distinct finished gown is acquired once; multiple scenes, corrections, visits, or family activities in the same gown are repeat appearances and not repeat purchases.
purchaseCanon.referenceExclusion: Dress-design reference inputs, photos, superseded edits, montage-only studies not showing a worn outfit, and unapproved generated illustrations never independently create a Daysha purchase.
purchaseCanon.valuationRule: Confirmed in-story acquisition is distinct from knowing the exact payment amount, payer, receipt identifier, or absolute calendar date. Unknown gold/date values never downgrade an acquired gown to an unverified purchase.
purchaseCanon.otherWearers: Garments worn or gifted to the Queen Mother are separate garments belonging to her, not automatically Daysha purchases.
purchaseCanon.uncertainMatch: If two illustrations show similar gowns, their acquired/owned status is canon, but matching them to one physical gown remains an identity-reconciliation task; do not invent an additional payment for an apparent repeat.
purchaseCanon.appliesTo: Approved story illustrations and established narrative wardrobe purchases.
